beats.care: If an Instagram page or DM promises sure-shot returns, it's a red flag. Check SEBI registration and never pay into their account.
beats.what: Hyderabad police said three people lost 5.35 crore rupees in a single day, including 52.51 lakh to a fake investment scheme that started on Instagram.
beats.why: Scammers pose as investment advisers or bosses and push quick transfers. Another victim lost 2.70 crore to a fake message from a CEO.

cards.body: You're added to a group full of fake 'winners', shown fake profit screenshots, then asked to deposit on an app or site they control. Withdrawals get blocked with new 'fees'.
cards.title: how the trick works

cards.body: Police Commissioner VC Sajjanar said once money moves, tracing and recovery are hard. If you're cheated, call 1930 or report on cybercrime.gov.in right away.

cards.q: What's the biggest red flag in an online investment pitch?
cards.why: Real investments carry risk; anyone promising sure profits is likely running a scam.

hook: 10 years of trading, then *one Instagram DM*. ₹52 lakh gone

learn.t: Experience doesn't protect you: this victim had traded stocks for nearly 10 years before an Instagram message lured him in.

sources.name: Telangana Today
sources.title: Hyderabad cyber frauds: three victims lose Rs 5.35 crore in one day

tldr: A Hyderabad trader with 10 years of stock market experience lost ₹52.51 lakh to a fake investment pitch that began on Instagram.
